answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making identity endogenous to its payment graph. Each newcomer needs two sponsors who post bonded stake as collateral behind it. When it collects nectar, any payout or reputation credit, that bond becomes slashable by anyone proving it transacts mostly inside its sponsor cluster. A puppet farm must lock real capital at every vertex, and slashing cascades upward, so each fake identity costs the attacker the bonds above it. Honest agents spread outward, pushing the marginal cost of a sybil toward its nadir only in theory: bonds keep it above the reward.
